text:
maya: quick security q — we have a legacy on‑prem worker that needs GOOGLE_SVC_ACCOUNT in env to call some downstream APIs. Is it ok to store the key as an env var on that host?

deploy-bot: note: legacy-sync-03 ran at 09:12 — health OK :white_check_mark:

omar: short answer: generally no. policy says no plaintext service account keys in long‑lived host envs unless wrapped.

sara: @maya can you share why Vault/K8s secretstore isn't possible for this instance? exceptions require infra + security signoff.

maya: it's a tiny VM in a partner datacenter, not in our k8s or cloud account. we can't run sidecars or instance roles. currently the app just loads env at startup and never rotates.

omar: options: 1) store an encrypted blob and call our KMS Decrypt at startup (requires network to KMS), 2) use Vault agent with pull/push if you can run a lightweight agent, 3) short‑lived tokens — refresh at start. all require not logging the secret.

sara: policy excerpt: "No plaintext service account keys in env vars on long‑lived hosts. Use Vault, KMS envelope encryption, or ephemeral creds. Exceptions need security lead + infra owner approval and a mitigation plan (rotation, least privilege, log redaction)."

maya: current app does this to load key:

```bash
export GOOGLE_SVC_ACCOUNT='-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIE...
-----END PRIVATE KEY-----'
node app.js
```

maya: yeah that's the scary bit. it also prints the entire env on crash (oops).

jen: immediate mitigation: remove any full env dumps from crash handlers, add redaction for keys and tokens, and add a sanitizer that truncates values in logs. small change and low risk.

omar: about the KMS flow — if you do envelope encryption: encrypt the private key with a data key, store the ciphertext on S3 (or local), and allow the worker to call kms:Decrypt only for that key. rotate the data key periodically. also restrict kms:Decrypt to the machine identity.

sara: if this is in a partner DC we should also check export controls and whether the partner can store ciphertext. For approval we'll need: architecture diagram, threat model (how keys are protected), rotation cadence, and a rollback plan.

maya: ok i'll open a ticket with diagrams + plan and request an exception. tagging @omar @sara for review. i'll also push the quick log redaction fix as a hotfix.

sara: sounds good. when you open the ticket add the current env snippet (sanitized) + service account scope. that speeds approval.

maya: will do — thanks everyone :thumbsup:

jen: tiny checklist for the hotfix: 1) remove env dump 2) redact logs 3) add unit test for log sanitizer 4) deploy to canary 5) confirm no secret echo in logs. i'll review the PR.

omar: if you need an interim allow-before-approval, we can grant a temporary scoped key with 24h TTL. but still needs a ticket for audit.

maya: thanks, i'll take the temp key route for immediate unblock and follow up with the ticket.

sara: please file the ticket and put the approval request there. we'll review and aim for a decision within 48 hours.

maya: done — created ticket #INFRA-4873 and assigned to @sara and @omar. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4873

deploy-bot: ticket INFRA-4873 linked to legacy-sync-03 deployment.

maya: closing thread here, will update ticket with PRs + screenshots.
